name: יְחֶזְקֵאל
gloss: El strengthens; or El is strong
summary: Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, to whom the word of Yahweh came among the exiles by the river Kebar, “and the hand of Yahweh was upon him there” (Ezk 1:3); his life was made a sign to the exiles (Ezk 24:24). Also Jehezkel, head of the twentieth course of priests in David's ordering (1Ch 24:16). The name is the verb חָזַק, imperfect, with אֵל: “El strengthens” or “El is strong”. Scripture does not explain it, but his commission is told in the root's words: Israel are “hard of face and strong of heart (חִזְקֵי־לֵב)” and “strong of forehead (חִזְקֵי־מֵצַח)”, and Yahweh answers, “I have made your face strong against their faces, and your forehead strong against their foreheads … do not fear them” (Ezk 2:4; 3:7–9); “the hand of Yahweh was strong (חָזָקָה) upon me” (Ezk 3:14).

evidence.note: “The word of Yahweh came to יְחֶזְקֵאל son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Kebar.”
“יְחֶזְקֵאל shall be a sign to you; according to all that he has done you shall do.”
“I have made your face חֲזָקִים against their faces, and your forehead חָזָק against their foreheads.”
“Like a diamond, harder than flint, I have made your forehead; do not fear them.”
“All the house of Israel חִזְקֵי־מֵצַח וּקְשֵׁי־לֵב הֵמָּה.”
“The sons are קְשֵׁי פָנִים וְחִזְקֵי־לֵב; I am sending you to them.”

note: Takes h.bs.aj (3 tokens: Ezk 1:3; 24:24; 1Ch 24:16). j.be.ai, a zero-token cross-reference filed as a verb with the lemma יְחֶזְקֵאל, is left unassigned. The form is the qal imperfect יֶחֱזַק with אֵל; since the qal is mostly intransitive, “El is strong” is as possible as “El strengthens” (the qal is transitive at Jer 20:7 and 2Ch 28:20). The link to Ezk 3:7–9 is a play on the root, not an explanation the text gives.
